skill.name: harness-building
skill.desc: Understanding context compilers - what they do, why you want one, how they work.
skill.overview:
A harness watches LLXML projects, assembles context based on profiles and selected items, and outputs compiled CTX files that LLMs read to start sessions. It's the bridge between your files and your agent.
Saddle is the reference implementation. This skill teaches the concepts; see the Saddle spec for implementation details.
skill.what:
A harness is a context compiler. It: - Discovers projects by scanning for `ll.xml` manifests - Watches META directories for changes - Compiles context based on profiles and selected items - Outputs assembled XML to `ctx/` for LLM consumption
Core loop: discover → watch → select → compile → output
skill.why:
LLMs need context. Manually copying files into prompts doesn't scale.
A harness automates this: - Change a file → harness recompiles - Select different items → different context - Switch profiles → different compilation rules - Add a project → harness discovers it
You focus on the work. The harness keeps context fresh.

concepts.profiles:
Profiles define what gets compiled. They specify: - Static includes (files, skills) - Dynamic queries (glob, git, tickets, recent) - Inheritance from other profiles - Injection point for selected items
Common profiles: `base`, `kickoff`, `reflection`, `ticket-work`
concepts.items:
Items are what you select for compilation: - Inbox items (forward-looking) - Retro items (backward-looking)
User selects items + profile → harness compiles → CTX output
concepts.queries: Dynamic queries resolved at compile time: - `glob` - File pattern matching - `tickets` - Tickets by status - `git` - Status, diff, log - `grep` - Content search - `recent` - Recent files by mtime
concepts.skills:
Skill resolution order: 1. Project skills - `META/skills/` (dev-time) or `main/skills/` (if configured) 2. Global skills - From projects with `skills global="true"` in ll.xml 3. Vendor skills - From vendored dependencies in `main/vendor/`
Global skills typically live in `main/skills/` so they can be vendored. Project-specific skills live in `META/skills/` and don't ship.
Profiles include skills by name, resolved through this chain.

skill.flow:
```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph Input I[Inbox Items] R[Retro Items] end
subgraph Compile S{Select Items} P[Profile] C[Compiler] CTX[CTX File] end
subgraph Conversation LLM[LLM Session] end
subgraph Outcomes T[Tickets] SK[Skill Edits] SP[Spec Changes] M[More Inbox] end
I --> S R --> S S --> P P --> C C --> CTX CTX --> LLM LLM --> T LLM --> SK LLM --> SP LLM --> M ```
skill.two_flows:
Forward-looking: inbox → kickoff CTX → conversation → outcomes
Used for: new work, processing ideas, answering questions
Backward-looking: retros → reflection CTX → conversation → outcomes
Used for: reviewing completed work, extracting patterns, updating skills
Both flows produce the same outcome types (tickets, skills, specs, more items). The difference is temporal orientation of the input.
skill.building_one:
If building your own harness:
1. **Discovery** - Scan dev roots for `ll.xml` files 2. **Watching** - Use platform file watcher on META directories 3. **Profile parsing** - Load and resolve profile inheritance 4. **Query execution** - Implement glob, git, tickets, etc. 5. **Compilation** - Assemble sections into single XML 6. **Output** - Write to `META/ctx/{profile}.xml`
The core value is the compilation loop. UI and features are optional.
skill.reference:
See the Saddle spec for a complete implementation: - `~/dev/apps/saddle/META/spec/saddle.xml`
Saddle implements all concepts here plus: - Tauri desktop app with React frontend - Kanban board for tickets - Profile and inbox editors - File watching with debounce - Token estimation
